intended_object: This is the finite set of counted rectangle–pentagon decompositions that share a terminal side, where the rectangle's left edge lies strictly inside the pentagon's column interval. Per the docstring and module docs, the set exists so these terms can be paired off and cancelled in characteristic two, inside the proof of the pentagon chain-map equation (commutation invariance of grid homology).
explanation: The definition filters `rectanglePentagonDecompositions` to keep the terms with a particular overlap configuration. Its only job is to index one family of terms in a characteristic-two cancellation argument within the commutation-invariance proof. Ozsváth–Stipsicz–Szabó, Section 5.1, does not treat this as a standard object; it is the kind of case split a proof uses internally. So it is an auxiliary construction for a proof, with no standalone mathematical counterpart. Its body matches the docstring: the right sides are equal (a common terminal side), and the rectangle's left side is strictly inside the pentagon's interval (`cIoo`).
